newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures skid late to big losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures skid late to big losses.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures skidded to hefty losses for a second consecutive session.
March Standard & Poor's 500 futures began eroding in earnest during the final 30 minutes and tumbled to their steepest loss after cash stocks had closed.
March futures ended at about a 2.50-point discount to cash after posting nearly as large a discount at Wednesday's close.

The sharp pullback capped an afternoon of range-trading at lower levels. Traders blamed the late slide partly on a slump in high-technology stocks and partly on rate-hike jitters that also spooked U.S. Treasury bond futures.

"The technology sector was absolutely destroyed. It just killed us," said one floor broker in S&P 500 futures. "The technology stocks had absolute leadership...(and) the cash (S&Ps) couldn't hold up."
The futures fall gained momentum from an influx of institutional selling that pumped up light, choppy afternoon trade that had been dominated by locals.
"We started to see some good paper in there late," the floor broker added.
Those inflows sent S&Ps tripping near the cash close below supports that had contained even Wednesday's 19-point selloff.
The March futures slunk below 797.50, also the 20-day moving average, and 797.00, near a cluster of old highs. It then quickly bumped below Wednesday's two-week low at 795.00.

Traders also said rumors circulated widely in debt and stock index futures markets that a Washington-based consulting group had issued a report saying the Federal Reserve would feel compelled to raise rates by 25 basis points to keep its inflation-fighting credibility after Fed chairman Greenspan's more hawkish bent in Humphrey-Hawkins testimony Wednesday.
Fed vice chairman Alice Rivlin's remarks Thursday repeated those she made Tuesday but still were seen adding weight.
Rivlin reiterated her view that the economy was doing fine and its biggest threat would be too much of a good thing.
Nearby S&P 500s early had firmed to the day's peak and resistance near 807.00 area, where selling by a few dealers slammed the contract back down toward unchanged.
It had chopped at mostly weaker levels, tracking moves in T-bond futures, until the late-afternoon selloff.

March S&P 500s slid 11.25 pts to 792.50, Value Lines fell 5.50 to 708.50, Nikkei rose 150.0 to 18,985.0, Midcap lost 3.55 to 261.80, NYSE Composite dropped 5.10 to 416.25, Russell lost 5.90 to 358.10, and Nasdaq fell 33.75 to 846.75. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
